# PRD 008: pods

**Schema**: pij/prd · **Source**: 008-pods.dd.json · **Sections**: 8

## Meta

| --- | --- |
| title | PRD 008: pods |
| status | draft |
| updated | 2026-11-25 |
| owner | pm-001 |
| summary | A pod is a group of role instances stood up together with shared parameters. A prime plans, starts, takes down and brings back a recurring group of seats with a few commands instead of handling each one by hand. |

<a id="why"></a>

## Why

Some groups of seats recur. A project manager, a coder and a reviewer build a step. A note taker, a researcher and a validator sit in on a call. Today each such group is set up by hand from a prose description: one fleet's prime listed what it repeats every time as the session folder, a packet for each seat, per-subject copies of the same roles, spawn commands with model flags, and a close checklist. Another fleet has started keeping a folder per seat and a list of seats to start from, but nothing in pij reads it. pij ships role templates one role at a time and has no way to store, share or stand up a group.

<a id="actors"></a>

## Actors

| id | name | need |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a-operator | operator | Say "set up a pod for this" and approve a short plan. |
| a-prime | prime | Stand up a known group of seats by choosing a template and filling in what differs this time. |
| a-holder | role holder | Start from what earlier seats in the same role learned about the same subject. |

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

| id | goal |
| --- | --- |
| g-1 | Standing up a recurring group of seats is plan, confirm, up; taking it down is one command that really stops it. |
| g-2 | What a pod's seats learn stays with their role and subject after the pod is gone. |

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non goals

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| n-1 | Replacing emergent communities. A pod is optional, and PRD 001 req-27 and req-28 still hold. |
| n-2 | A second way of running steps. A pod's start and close steps are procedures (PRD 005). |
| n-3 | Starting, configuring or stopping seats the pod only consults, or seats in another fleet. |
| n-4 | Shipping, sharing and adopting templates. That is PRD 010; this PRD needs only a definition folder to read. |
| n-5 | Walls between pods. pij does not stop a pod's seats reading earlier runs; a template that wants them not to says so in its seed text (honesty, not enforcement; Jordan's ruling 2026-11-25, round 2, ruling 5). |
| n-6 | Creating a run's branch or worktree. `pod up` creates neither; a template carries the procedure that does (Jordan's ruling 2026-11-25, round 2, ruling 9). |
| n-7 | Access control on reading a pod: no observer role, no membership test, no hidden pod (Jordan's ruling 2026-11-25, round 2, ruling 8). |

| req-01 | A pod groups roles stood up together | A pod is a named group of role instances inside one community, with parameters set once for the group. A seat is in one pod or in none: pods are optional, and a seat that several pods rely on, such as a shared expert, belongs to none of them. A fleet may still put its experts in a pod of their own to manage them together. `pij pod show &lt;pod&gt;` shows a pod's members, their types, seats and states, how they feed each other and which outside roles it consults. Several pods from one template can run at the same time. The words are "pod" (the running group) and "pod template" (what it is made from), as in Kubernetes, and no others: there is no "pod instance", and no further Kubernetes concepts are brought in. | prime | must | [x] shipped | Two pods started from one template with different parameters both appear in `pij pod show`, each with its own members; a seat already in one pod is refused by a second, naming the first; and a role both pods consult appears under each as consulted, not as a member. | operator ruling 2026-11-25: the group is called a pod; operator ruling 2026-11-25: an expert shared between pods is in neither, and not everything needs to be in a pod | — | — |
| req-02 | A pod is defined by a folder | A pod is made from a pod template: a folder holding its parameters, its slots, how the slots feed each other, the text each slot is told at start, the outside roles the pod consults, and its deliverables. Every slot is a seat the pod starts. A consulted role is not a member: the pod names it so its seats know who to ask, and the pod never starts, configures or stops it. Each slot names only the parameters it needs, and may name the tools it needs and a slot whose model it must not share. A consulted role may be marked as needed before `up`. Each deliverable names the role that owns it, its stages and any role it is written back to. Every pod command takes the template's path, so a template can sit in the main repo (a fleet shared as files) or in governance; pij does not enforce where it lives. | template author | must | [x] shipped | A template with two slots, one consulted role and one deliverable validates from a path in the main repo and from one in governance; a slot that names a parameter the template does not declare is refused by name. | operator, 2026-11-25: parameters change depending on the seat's requirements; operator ruling 2026-11-25: an expert shared between pods is in neither, and not everything needs to be in a pod | — | — |
| req-03 | Plan shows everything and changes nothing | `pij pod plan &lt;template-path&gt; --set &lt;name&gt;=&lt;value&gt;` prints the seats it would start with their models, each seat's first turn, each role the pod consults and whether that role has a live holder, each deliverable and its owner, and everything `up` would warn about, each with the command that fixes it: a consulted role needed before `up` with no live holder, a reviewing slot on the same model as the slot it reviews, a deliverable whose owner role does not exist, and the tools each slot will be checked for. | req-04 | Up stands the pod up, together or one seat at a time | `pij pod up &lt;template-path&gt; --set …` creates the pod, starts each slot's seat as `pij spawn --as role:&lt;id&gt;` does (PRD 007), once per slot, and reports each slot as ready, degraded or failed. It warns and still starts: each warning (req-18, req-19, req-21) is printed with its fix and written to the pod's log. `up` creates no branch and no worktree; a template that needs them carries the procedure that makes them. `--no-start` creates the pod only, and each member is then started on its own with `pij spawn --as role:&lt;id&gt; --pod &lt;pod&gt;`. | prime | must | [x] shipped | `up` on a three-slot template reports three slots with their seats; with a consulted role needed before `up` absent, `up` still starts every slot and the pod's log holds the warning; no branch or worktree is created; with `--no-start` no seat is launched and each member starts individually into the same pod. | operator, 2026-11-25: the prime might still like to fire them up separately | — | — |
